evidence.claim: Home Depot's 2025 annual report says its Pro customers include professional renovators/remodelers, general contractors, maintenance professionals, handymen, property managers, building service contractors, and specialty tradespeople; these customers build, renovate, remodel, repair, and maintain residential properties.

Home Depot reported Q1 fiscal 2026 sales of $41.8 billion, up 4.8% year over year, and management said underlying demand was similar to fiscal 2025 despite consumer uncertainty and housing affordability pressure.
evidence.source_title: The Home Depot Announces First Quarter Fiscal 2026 Results; Reaffirms Fiscal 2026 Guidance

evidence.claim: Lowe's 2025 annual report says it serves DIY, DIFM, and Pro customers, including tradespeople, repair and remodelers, and property managers; it also says demand indicators include age of housing stock and housing turnover.

Ferguson describes its U.S. segment as providing plumbing, appliances, HVAC, fire, fabrication, infrastructure, and related products to residential and non-residential contractors, and states that it serves repair and remodel projects.
Ferguson reported fiscal 2025 net sales of $30.8 billion and said residential end markets were approximately half of U.S. revenue, while repair, maintenance, and improvement work remained soft.
evidence.source_title: Ferguson Reports Fourth Quarter and Year End Results

evidence.claim: Watsco describes itself as the leading distributor in the HVAC/R marketplace, serving more than 375,000 contractors, technicians, and installers from 693 locations across the U.S., Canada, and Latin America.
evidence.source_title: Watsco’s First Quarter Reflects Large-Scale Product Transition, Strong Sales Growth and Expanded Margins in Core Replacement Market

evidence.claim: Watsco reported that its fourth and first quarters are highly seasonal due to the timing of HVAC system replacement, supporting replacement-cycle relevance to the node.
evidence.source_title: Watsco Reports Record Full-Year Gross Margin, Meets Inventory Reduction Target and Generates Record 4th Quarter Cash Flow in Challenging Market Conditions

evidence.claim: Invitation Homes reported Q1 2026 total revenues of $734 million and property operating and maintenance costs of $251 million, up 5.8% year over year.
evidence.source_title: Invitation Homes Reports First Quarter 2026 Results

evidence.claim: Invitation Homes ended Q1 2026 with 85,970 wholly owned homes, making it a scaled recurring buyer of maintenance, repair, and turnover services.
evidence.source_title: Invitation Homes Reports First Quarter 2026 Results

evidence.claim: Morningstar DBRS said the U.S. home improvement sector in 2026 is likely to remain constrained by weak consumer sentiment, elevated mortgage rates, and low housing turnover, with growth skewed toward need-based repair and maintenance rather than discretionary remodeling.
evidence.source_title: U.S. Home Improvement Sector: Cautious Consumers and Housing Affordability Pressures Dampen Volume-Led Recovery in 2026

memory_update.text: Core public-market candidates for housing repair/remodel substitution node: HD, LOW, FERG, WSO, INVH.
Best direct mappings are Pro-focused home improvement retail, plumbing/HVAC distribution, HVAC replacement distribution, and institutional single-family rental maintenance demand.

Not yet covered in this five-name pass: paint/flooring specialists such as SHW and FND, appliance makers such as WHR, home-services platforms such as ANGI, storage/moving names, and smaller repair-service consolidators.
Need a later pass to separate necessary repair/maintenance exposure from discretionary remodel/furnishings exposure and to quantify Pro versus DIY mix by company.

node: Housing-linked consumer spend: home improvement, repair, maintenance, furnishings, rentership, and home services
summary: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the housing repair/remodel substitution node. The strongest direct exposures are large home-improvement retailers with Pro and repair/remodel demand, specialized plumbing/HVAC distributors tied to replacement and contractor capacity, and scaled single-family rental asset owners whose maintenance capex creates recurring downstream demand. This is a research universe only, not a buy/sell list.
